story_type: lava pouring into the ocean, steam wall beside homes
hook: This wall of steam is lava pouring into the ocean.
narration: This wall of steam is lava pouring into the Pacific along half a mile of coastline.
On June fourth, 2018, a USGS helicopter flew over Kapoho Bay on Hawaii's Big Island.
By six fifteen that morning, lava from fissure eight had been entering the ocean for more than seven hours.
When lava hits seawater, the water flashes to steam, carrying acid and tiny shards of volcanic glass. Scientists call it laze.
[short pause] Look at the houses along the shore, right beside it.
outcome: By afternoon, lava was filling the shallow bay, building new land out into the water.
title: Lava pours into a Hawaii bay
description:
Lava from Kilauea's fissure 8 poured into Kapoho Bay on Hawaii's Big Island on June 4, 2018, building a delta and sending a laze plume along the coast, seen from a USGS helicopter overflight.
